chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abi Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Jews asked the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying: Relate for us the genealogy of your Lord.
He remained three days not answering them
Say: He is Allah the One

key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Say: He is Allah the One

ai.seo_question: Why did the Jews ask the Prophet for his Lord's genealogy and what was the response?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the Jewish inquiry into the 'genealogy' (nasab) of God, a concept rooted in their anthropomorphic understanding of divine lineage, which prompted the revelation of Surah Al-Ikhlas. The three-day pause signifies the gravity of the question and the divine preparation of a concise theological response that negates physical generation or begetting. In Shia scholarship, this is often linked to the principle of Tawhid al-Dhat, emphasizing that God’s essence is unique and incomparable, distinct from created beings who possess lineage.

en.ammaar-muslim: 6. [6/303] al-Kafi: Ahmad b. Idris from Muhammad b. Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan b. Yahya from Abi Ayyub from Muhammad b. Muslim from Abi Abdillahعليه السلام  who said:
The Jews asked the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله saying: Relate for us the genealogy of your Lord.
He (the prophet) remained three days not answering them
then it was revealed “Say: He is Allah the One”
